text:
rachel: Quick thread: cert pinning for ephemeral peering endpoints. do we want short-lived certs tied to ENI lifecycle or keep long-lived tenant certs?
priya: short-lived certs reduce blast radius but add rotation complexity. leaning short-lived for per-tenant ENIs.
sam: agree but need automated CSR flow and a signer service. otherwise ops will drown.
luca: we can reuse our existing CA service with a "peering" role that mints certs valid for e.g. 1h and requires proof-of-possession from the agent.
rachel: good. how do we handle validation for shared endpoints during transition? clients might still present long-lived certs.
priya: controlplane should accept both verifier chains for a migration window: long-lived tenant cert OR short-lived peer cert bound to ENI id. record both in registry.
sam: add audit: every short-lived cert issuance must be logged to tenant-migration-log and tied to migration task id. makes rollback easier.
ops-bot: note: signer-service scheduled maintenance 03:00-03:30 UTC tomorrow. expect brief CA restarts.
luca: plan: implement CSR+POAP endpoint, 1h cert TTL, registry writes, dual-accept mode, and an automated revoke path. I'll post a spike PR next week.
priya: i'll include this in the runbook and add failure modes: CA outage, clock skew on agents, revoked certs still cached. include mitigations.
rachel: thanks team. this should make ephemeral peering much safer.
